text: Five clues that one fur trader was hiding a huge secret.
A young recruit called John Fubbister signs up for three years, at eight pounds a year.
A ship carries him to Canada, to the fur forts of the Hudson's Bay Company.
Clue four: he hauls freight and chops wood, like the rest of the men.
Clue three: he paddles almost three thousand kilometres by canoe, and keeps up.
Clue two: winter, eighteen-oh-seven. A trip south to Pembina, on the Red River.
Clue one: December twenty-ninth. At a rival post, John asks to rest by the fire.
The trader finds him on the hearth, crying out in pain.
John is a woman, Isobel Gunn. And within an hour, she gives birth to a baby boy.
Women were banned from the posts. So the company made her a washerwoman,
and in eighteen-oh-nine, it shipped her home.
Her boss admitted she worked at anything, as well as the men.
History remembers who was allowed to do the job, not who could.
Would you have kept her secret?
